question: Ticket 3f544e08a783 says "The ticket says 'Find why ... reds and fix it so that the proof reseals green' without requiring that if the tooth (test case) changes, the decision be recorded in the same act as the change.", but outline 9.4.2.3.7.6 reads "A red is first a question: is the code wrong, or is the tooth measuring the wrong thing? An LLM reads the work against the component's why, the tooth's why and CP1-CP6, because even the Laws rest finally on the core principles. Either the code or the tooth changes, and a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6). A tooth a hollow build could pass is worthless at every tier (Law 8)." (The outline mandates 'a tooth change carries that decision in the same act (corrosion, 17.11.6)'. The ticket's falsifier only requires the proof to reseal green, not that any decision be carried if the tooth is modified. A builder following the ticket exactly could change the tooth without recording the decision, violating both the corrosion requirement and preventing the system from learning why the tooth changed.). Which stands, the ticket or the outline?
why_it_blocks: the ticket and the component outline disagree; building it would build one of them wrong
